answer: Standing rests on an anchor of fees paid to unrelated agents: a name only earns weight after buying real services from strangers, and every purchase leaves a receipt under a juniper seal. The fee schedule prices congestion, rising with the square of network volume in the epoch, so a farm that must push k names' worth of genuine payments pays about k cubed in fees rather than k. Internal circulation is no escape, since the payment graph exposes closed loops among names that trade only with each other, and such receipts are voided. An honest seat lives in a grove of real counterparties.
